entries.english:
1286, 29 June, Hohenfurt. — Heinrich von Rosenberg and Albert von Payre repeat their gift of the church in Strobnitz to Hohenfurt Abbey.

XXXIV. The peace of God’s house is carefully and prudently provided for when what is done for its benefit and honor is committed in writing, as a reliable instrument, to the knowledge of posterity. Therefore, we, Heinrich von Rosenberg and Albert von Borschowe, wish to make known to all who hear these presents, now and in the future, that after deliberation and mature counsel, by equal vote and unanimous consent, with the full and proper approval of our wives and predecessors, we have given and conveyed, by joined and authoritative hands and as a free gift, the right of patronage of the church in Strobnitz—which was recognized as belonging to us by rightful inheritance and hereditary succession—with all its endowments, tithes, and other appurtenances, known and yet to be discovered, in full right, as our forebears possessed it for many years, to the church of Saint Mary the Virgin at Hohenfurt and the brethren who continually serve God there. We grant it under a rightful title of ownership, to be held peacefully and freely in perpetuity, so that, through this great alms-gift, by providing for the brethren from the goods bestowed on us by God, they may be more freely devoted to divine worship and serve the Lord more fervently and beneficially for the salvation of the living and the dead.

So that no claim by our heirs or friends may ever disturb this solemn and generous gift, we have issued these present letters, written concerning it, to the aforesaid monastery at Hohenfurt and its brethren, secured by our seals and the testimony of the witnesses listed below. The witnesses are: Lord Berhtold, dean of Strobnitz; Lord Chunrad, parish priest of Ragiz; Lord Jacob, parish priest of Rosenberg; Andreas of Hossitz; Roger of Laichenbach; Heinrich of Altenburg; Conasch of Strizendorf; Nedamir of Bschizawiz; the brothers Ulrich and Bschedworius, called von Weihsei; Schenco and his son Dwursrad of Metliz; Wazlav, son of Henate; and many others.

Given and enacted at Hohenfurt in the year of the Lord 1286, on the feast of the Apostles Peter and Paul.

Seals: Heinrich von Rosenberg’s seal, as in no. XXXIII, somewhat damaged and formerly suspended on green and red silk; Albert von Stropnitz’s well-preserved seal, formerly suspended on green silk threads. Compare no. XXXIII. Millauer, p. 90, no. 18; Trajer, ibid., p. 367; both give the incorrect year 1287.
